concepts.learning_objective: Identify cellular, tissue, organ and organ-system levels of organisation with examples.
Distinguish complete from incomplete digestive systems and open from closed circulatory systems.
Distinguish asymmetrical, radially symmetrical and bilaterally symmetrical body plans.

topics.title: Germ layers, coelom, segmentation and notochord

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish diploblastic from triploblastic animals on the basis of embryonic layers.
Classify animals as coelomates, pseudocoelomates or acoelomates from the nature of the body cavity.
Explain metameric segmentation and the notochord as bases of classification.
Describe the water canal system, skeleton and reproduction of sponges.
Explain cnidoblasts, polyp and medusa forms and metagenesis in cnidarians.
Identify the distinctive features of ctenophores such as comb plates and bioluminescence.
Describe the features and parasitic adaptations of flatworms.
Describe the pseudocoelomate body plan and features of roundworms.
Describe metamerism, circulation, excretion and reproduction in annelids.
Describe the features and economically important examples of arthropods.
Describe the body plan of molluscs including mantle, shell and radula.
Describe the water vascular system of echinoderms and the body plan of hemichordates.
State the fundamental characters that distinguish chordates from non-chordates.
Compare urochordates, cephalochordates and vertebrates on the basis of the notochord.
Compare cyclostomes, cartilaginous fishes and bony fishes.

topics.title: Tetrapoda: Amphibia, Reptilia, Aves and Mammalia

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the distinguishing features of amphibians and reptiles.
Describe the features of birds, including those that help in flight.
Identify the unique features of mammals and classify examples.
